text:
Maria (Customer): hey team, we're getting a bunch of 429s and slow responses since yesterday afternoon — started around 2026-03-14 20:10 UTC. looks related to a spike in traffic but the errors reference per-model limits. example response: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests\n{\n  \"error\":{\"type\":\"rate_limit_exceeded\",\"message\":\"Per-model RPM exceeded\",\"details\":{\"model\":\"redwood-v2-xl\",\"limit_type\":\"per_model_rpm\",\"limit\":1200,\"window_seconds\":60}},\"request_id\":\"req_9f3b2a\"\n}`
Can someone confirm the RPM/TPM/concurrency limits for `redwood-v2-xl` on our hosted plan? We're also seeing lots of retries ballooning cost.

Alex (Support): hey @Maria, sorry about that — can you paste the full curl you used (no secrets) and the org id/account id? also, do you see any `X-RateLimit-*` headers in the responses? those help a lot.

Maria (Customer): org id: org_87a2c. sample curl (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v2-xl","input":"<long chat history>...","max_tokens":1024,"temperature":0.2}'
```
Response headers I captured: `X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `X-RateLimit-Reset: 16` (seconds). body is the 429 above. We also saw some `504 Gateway Timeout` when concurrency seems high.

Alex (Support): thanks — that makes it clearer. initial triage notes:
- `X-RateLimit-Limit` matches a per-model RPM cap (requests per minute).
- you also might be hitting TPM (tokens per minute) if you have large context + long responses. TPM is enforced separately.
- concurrency limits can cause upstream queueing which leads to timeouts when requests wait too long.

Jordan (SRE): jumping in — for hosted customers on the Standard tier, `redwood-v2-xl` defaults are approximately: `per_model_rpm=1200`, `per_model_tpm=1_000_000` (tokens/min), and `max_concurrency=60`. those numbers can vary by org/plan and there are burst smoothing windows. the 504s are consistent with our frontend queue hitting concurrency caps and a request timing out upstream.

Maria (Customer): is there a way to see per-org consumption breakdown so I can prove whether it's RPM or TPM causing the block? our dashboard only shows aggregate tokens but not per-model rpm/tpm.

Alex (Support): we can pull the audit logs for your org and show the per-model metrics. I'll request them now — @Jordan can you attach the last 1 hour consumption for org_87a2c?

Jordan (SRE): attaching results (summary lines):
- total requests last 60m: 4,520
- requests to redwood-v2-xl: 2,140 (avg RPM ~2140)
- tokens consumed last 60m: 1,890,000 (tokens/min peaks ~42k)
- concurrency peaks: 78 concurrent requests
So yes — your requests to `redwood-v2-xl` exceeded the per-model RPM of 1200 and also peaked above the per-org max_concurrency of 60. both triggers explain the 429s and some upstream 504s. request IDs with 429: `req_9f3b2a`, `req_9f3b9c`, `req_9f3c14` (timestamps included in full export).

Maria (Customer): ohhh that's great to have. the spike is from a background job that retried aggressively after transient fails — so retries amplified the spike. what do we do short-term to stop the bleeding?

Alex (Support): short-term mitigation options:
- throttle your background job clients to a lower RPS and add jitter/exponential backoff. avoid immediate retries; use 429 retry-after header when present.
- reduce max_tokens and prune chat history to cut TPM. try truncating oldest messages or using summaries.
- route some requests to a cheaper/smaller model variant (e.g., `redwood-v2-large`) during bursts.
- temporarily pause non-critical background jobs while we stabilize.

Jordan (SRE): medium-term / config options we can offer:
- request a quota increase for per-model RPM and concurrency (subject to safety checks).
- enable a controlled burst credit for your org for short windows (we can grant 2x for 5 minutes once after review).
- enable smart client-side throttling rules via our SDK: token-aware rate limiter that counts tokens rather than just requests.

Maria (Customer): can you give an ETA to get a temporary bump? we need to avoid revenue-impacting downtime.

Alex (Support): I've opened an internal escalation (INC-2026-1458) to request a temporary per-model RPM bump and a one-time concurrency raise. @Jordan — can SRE approve a 2x RPM bump for 30 minutes and bump concurrency to 120 for org_87a2c?

Jordan (SRE): I can approve a one-time emergency bump after we verify there's no abuse. I ran a quick check on end-user IP distribution and didn't see obvious scraping patterns. I'll apply a 2x RPM bump for 30 minutes (effective in ~3 minutes) and increase concurrency to 120 for the same window. will notify when done.

ratebot: [system] applied quota-modification: org=org_87a2c change={per_model_rpm:1200->2400, max_concurrency:60->120} expires_in=1800s request_id=req_9f4a00

Alex (Support): Maria can you confirm whether the errors drop off in the next 10 minutes? also please capture any `Retry-After` headers if present.

Maria (Customer): seeing fewer 429s already, latency back to normal, thanks. one more thing — our finance team saw a spike in billing because retries increased token counts. can billing help?

billing-bot: hi @Maria — please file a billing dispute with invoice id `inv_2026_03_14_7782` referencing this thread and INC-2026-1458. for quick handling, include the request ids you believe are duplicate-retry related and an estimate of tokens retried. we'll prioritize review for EMERGENCY adjustments.

Maria (Customer): will do, thx.

Alex (Support): final follow-ups/takeaways:
- root cause: background job retry storm + per-model RPM + concurrency caps => 429s & timeouts. TPM pressure also contributing due to long context.
- immediate fixes: we applied a temporary quota bump, pause/reduce retries, route some load to smaller model, trim contexts.
- next steps for us: SRE will monitor and we can request a permanent quota increase if traffic pattern persists. Support to coordinate billing dispute.

Jordan (SRE): also note: if you often send very long contexts near the model limit (e.g., >60k tokens for large context models), we will start rejecting with a `context_length_exceeded` error (HTTP 400) rather than treating it as a rate event. that is separate from RPM/TPM and needs client truncation or summarization.

Maria (Customer): super helpful — thanks everyone. we'll add client-side token-aware throttling and better retry backoff. ping me if you need anything else. :wave:

Alex (Support): closing the immediate incident but keeping the ticket open for billing + quota follow-up. I'm adding a short runbook note in your org's support workspace summarizing mitigation steps. :thumbsup:
